formulas.formula: Never miss a due date again: every bill, every month, ticked off as you pay.
1. Bills: type the year, then every bill once: amount, due day, how often and (for bills that aren't monthly) the first month it's due.
2. Checklist: tick the box when you pay a bill. Grey boxes mean that bill isn't due that month.
3. Upcoming: everything due in the next 30 days, plus anything overdue, in date order.
4. Calendar: pick a month to see every bill on its due day, like a wall calendar.
5. Year Summary: every bill and category, month by month.
6. Dashboard: this month and your whole year at a glance.
Leave it blank on Bills: the sheet uses today. The example uses Sep 15, 2027.
Pick How Often, then the First Month it's due. The rest is worked out for you.
In shorter months the bill lands on the last day of the month.
On Checklist, untick the boxes. On Bills, type over the example bills.
Tinted cells: these calculate for you.
Yellow: due in the next 7 days.
Red: overdue, or something to check.
Grey: that bill isn't due that month.
Thank you for your purchase! Here's to a year with zero late fees.
=IF(TRIM('Bills'!C6&"")="","Your bills at a glance.",'Bills'!C6&"'s bills at a glance.")
Pick a month. Blank = this month.
List every bill once. The Checklist, Calendar, Upcoming and Dashboard all read from here.
Tick a box when you pay that bill. Grey = not due that month. Red = overdue. Yellow = due within 7 days.
Bills due in the next 30 days, plus anything overdue, soonest first. Paid ones turn green.
Every bill on its due day. Pick a month. Tick bills as paid on the Checklist.
Pick from the list. Blank = this month.
Green: paid.  Yellow: due in the next 7 days.  Red: overdue.  Grey: another month.
What each bill costs, month by month. Paid comes from the ticks on Checklist.
